paper_metadata.title: A Practical Quantum Solver for Multidimensional Partial Differential Equations

experiments.description: Hybrid PDE solver using FDM + C2Q + numerical instantiation for multidimensional Poisson equations, evaluated on 1D, 2D, and 3D Poisson cases across simulators and IBM real hardware.

algorithm.variant: Variant 1: FDM + classical-to-quantum (C2Q) encoding + numerical instantiation

hyperparameters.encoding: C2Q amplitude-style encoding of normalized vector

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical discretized PDE vector is normalized and encoded into quantum state via C2Q; FDM converts PDE to Au=b; polar decomposition/SVD used to obtain unitary component for quantum implementation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve Au = b after FDM discretization and polar decomposition A = PU, then recover u from the measured output state.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Boundary values set to zero for multidimensional Poisson cases.

problem_instance.description: Multidimensional Poisson equation benchmark cases, including 1D with source f(x)=10 and boundary values ux0=-0.6, uxNx=0.7; 2D with source f(x,y)=xy and zero boundary values; 3D with source f(x,y,z)=xyz and zero boundary values.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic PDE test functions on discretized grids; 1D, 2D, and 3D Poisson configurations.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Finite-difference discretization; normalization of input vector; SVD/polar decomposition preprocessing.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared solution profiles, RMSE, and total execution time against classical and VQE-based baselines on statevector simulator, AerSimulator, and ibm_torino; 1M shots for simulator runs and 0.1M shots on hardware for 1D Poisson.

noise_model.noise_description: AerSimulator noisy simulation; real hardware noise on ibm_torino

classical_postprocessing: Recovery of solution vector from measured amplitudes

speedup_claims.conditions: noise-free and noisy simulators; real quantum hardware for some cases
speedup_claims.caveats: No numeric speedup factor reported in the text.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: FFT-based classical PDE solvers O(N log N)
speedup_claims.conditions: Variant 1 circuit depth complexity, where N = 2^n
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a depth-complexity comparison, not a wall-clock runtime benchmark.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(N log N) for FFT-based classical PDE solvers

experiments.description: Hybrid PDE solver using FDM + C2Q + column-by-column decomposition for multidimensional Poisson equations, evaluated on 2D Poisson with noisy simulator.

algorithm.variant: Variant 2: FDM + classical-to-quantum (C2Q) encoding + column-by-column decomposition (CCD)

hyperparameters.encoding: C2Q amplitude-style encoding of normalized vector

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical discretized PDE vector encoded via C2Q; unitary implemented via CCD from isometries.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve Au = b after FDM discretization and polar decomposition A = PU, then recover u from the measured output state.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Boundary values set to zero for 2D Poisson.

problem_instance.description: 2D Poisson equation with source function f(x,y)=xy and zero boundary values.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic 2D Poisson benchmark on a grid with Nx=Ny=128 for classical reference; quantum run reported at 14 qubits.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Finite-difference discretization; normalization; SVD/polar decomposition preprocessing.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared solution profile on noisy simulator against classical benchmark; RMSE and runtime reported.

classical_postprocessing: Recovery of solution vector from measured amplitudes

experiments.description: Hybrid PDE solver for multidimensional heat equations using Variant 2 (FDM + C2Q + CCD), evaluated on 2D and 3D heat equations on noisy simulator.

algorithm.variant: Variant 2: FDM + classical-to-quantum (C2Q) encoding + column-by-column decomposition (CCD)

hyperparameters.encoding: C2Q amplitude-style encoding of normalized vector

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical discretized heat-equation system encoded via C2Q; unitary implemented via CCD.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve discretized heat equation Au=b after FDM and preprocessing.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Boundary values set to zero; initial condition specified at t=0.

problem_instance.description: 2D heat equation with initial condition f(x,0)=100°C, thermal diffusivity 0.97 cm^2/s (aluminum), domain length 100 cm, time duration 10 minutes, boundary values 0°C; 3D heat equation with initial condition f(x,y,0)=100°C, thermal diffusivities 0.97 cm^2/s along x and y, domain lengths 100 cm, time duration 10 minutes, boundary values 0°C.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic PDE benchmark grids; classical references shown for Nx=Nt=128 (2D) and Nx=Ny=Nt=16 (3D).

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Finite-difference discretization; normalization; SVD/polar decomposition preprocessing.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared solution profiles, RMSE, and total time against classical and VQE-based baselines; 256M shots for 2D noisy run and 1M shots for 3D noisy run.

classical_postprocessing: Recovery of solution vector from measured amplitudes

speedup_claims.conditions: 2D and 3D heat equations on noisy simulator

experiments.description: Hybrid PDE solver for Black-Scholes call option pricing using Variant 2 (FDM + C2Q + CCD), evaluated on small and larger discretizations and compared with VQE baseline.

algorithm.variant: Variant 2: FDM + classical-to-quantum (C2Q) encoding + column-by-column decomposition (CCD)

hyperparameters.encoding: C2Q amplitude-style encoding of normalized vector

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Discretized Black-Scholes PDE mapped to linear system Au=b; C2Q used to encode the classical vector.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Solve discretized Black-Scholes equation for call option pricing.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Boundary values set by option payoff and asymptotic boundary conditions.

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing with strike price K=$100, risk-free rate r=4.37, volatility 0.207, maturity 3 months, share price range 0<S_i<$400.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic Black-Scholes benchmark; price range follows the 4K rule; classical reference shown for Nx=Nt=4 and Nx=Nt=128.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Finite-difference discretization; payoff boundary conditions; normalization; SVD/polar decomposition preprocessing.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared solution profiles, RMSE, and total time against classical and VQE-based baselines on noisy simulator; 1M shots reported.

classical_postprocessing: Recovery of solution vector from measured amplitudes

speedup_claims.conditions: Black-Scholes call option on noisy simulator

scalability_data.problem_size: Black-Scholes call option, Nx=Nt=128 classical reference

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Discretized Navier-Stokes momentum equation mapped to linear system; C2Q used to encode the classical vector.

problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Boundary/initial conditions specified for velocity and pressure gradient.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic PDE benchmark; classical reference shown for Nx=Nt=128.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Finite-difference discretization; normalization; SVD/polar decomposition preprocessing.
